newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kloeckner-Werke sees small profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Kloeckner-Werke sees small profit rise.

text.p: German engineering group Kloeckner-Werke AG on Thursday predicted a small rise in profits in the business year to the end of September after a rise in sales and orders in the first five months.

Chairman Heinz-Ludwig Schmitz told shareholders in Duisburg pre-tax profit would "certainly be 200 million marks" and group profit on ordinary activities would be at least 50 million marks this year, up from 49.3 million marks the year before.
In the 1995/96 business year, Kloeckner posted net income of 700,000 marks, it first profit after years of losses.
Schmitz said group sales in the first five months of the new business year totalled 1.7 billion marks and incoming orders were 1.8 billion marks.

Adjusted to reflect the sale of the company's Kautex Gruppe division, sales and orders were both higher than the previous year, but the company gave no figures from the previous year adjusted to compare with the new business period.

Schmitz said that after "a 25-year dry spell" the company wanted to be able to resume paying a dividend in three years. To do this it needed to halve the losses it carries over to the next business year that now total 340 million marks.
